key_insight: Drift-diffusion optimization shows Cu2SiSe3 and Cu2SnS3 ternary chalcogenides can deliver competitive solar-cell performance, with a tandem stack outperforming either single junction alone.
engineering_relevance: This work identifies low-complexity Cu-based absorbers as promising candidates for high-efficiency, potentially scalable photovoltaic device design.
method: Drift-diffusion modeling of single-junction and two-terminal tandem solar cells
Swept absorber thickness, intrinsic carrier concentration, defect density, and interfacial band alignment
Evaluated buffer-layer effects and optimized Cu2SiSe3/Cu2SnS3 device architectures
evidence_signal: The optimized Cu2SiSe3 single junction reached 18.13% efficiency, Cu2SnS3 reached 15.59%, and the tandem architecture achieved 24.1% with 1.24 V VOC and 79.2% FF.
watch_item: These results are simulation-based, so real-device performance may be limited by materials quality, interface defects, and fabrication control.
paper_title: Photovoltaic Possibility of Cu2SiSe3 and Cu2SnS3 Ternary Chalcogenides- Single Junction to Tandem Architecture
